foundations.statement: Haar existence and finite-positive-scalar uniqueness, quotient Haar theorem with Borel sections/cutoffs on lcsc closed unimodular quotients, Tonelli and Bochner Fubini, dominated convergence, and elementary radial integration. The weak-measure promotion is the inherited numbered proof AMD8; product normalization and every exchange used here are proved explicitly.

Harish-Chandra admissibility: an irreducible unitary representation of a real reductive group has finite-dimensional maximal-compact isotypic spaces. This is the same separately named foundation as in RFD1. It supplies finite dimension in BWP4; the compact reproducer is then proved by an approximate identity and Cayley-Hamilton. No universal Bessel or lowest-type theorem is imported.
foundations.source_location: Armand Borel, Automorphic forms on reductive groups, printed Section10 paragraph labelled8.5, printed page27; general finite-component extension on page28.

foundations.statement: Finite-dimensional matrix and compact-group representation theory, Cayley-Hamilton, continuous approximate identities, and tensor products of finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.

The original ranks, parameters, numerical setting, IsDS/IsDSHpk and lowest vectors, given compact representations, original weak Haar measures and quotient identities, and given setting blocks wherever their original contracts quantify them. The final setting corollary preserves the supplied Forms0(D,D.u0) scope of ASG.

The entire source BesselNVGap at SettingBlocks.lean406–423: all original k,r,z,c,u,v,b, interlacing, half-integrality and cubic gap assumptions, every original IsDSHpk/IsHCTypeW and lowest unit vector, every weak Haar pair, and some x,x0 with the literal endomorphism-valued Bessel integral nonzero. Used explicitly in BWP14 and downstream; this chapter does not prove it.
